paper_title: Pyrene-1,5,6,10-tetracarboxyl diimide: a new building block for high-performance electrontransporting polymers

knowledge_points.content: The synthesis of 1,5,6,10-pyrene-tetracarboxyl diimide (PyDI) with six-membered rings was achieved by directing the ring-closure from the K-region (4,9-positions) to the non-K-region to avoid the formation of five-membered rings.
knowledge_points.evidence: Hence, a synthetic route featuring a ring-closure direction from the K- to non-K regions was subsequently investigated. This pathway necessarily entailed 4,9-bisfunctionalized pyrene derivatives as the precursor.

knowledge_points.content: The 1,5,6,10-PyDI derivatives exhibit LUMO levels around -3.7 eV, which are 0.2 to 0.4 eV lower than previously reported pyrene diimide isomers featuring five-membered rings.
knowledge_points.evidence: The corresponding LUMO levels are determined to be around -3.7 eV for both PyDIs, which are lowered by 0.2 to 0.4 eV compared to those previously reported for other 1,5,6,10-PyDI isomers.

knowledge_points.content: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of PyDI-C6 reveals a rigid and planar polycyclic scaffold with a short $\pi-\pi$ stacking distance of 3.20 Å and a slipped face-to-face packing motif.
knowledge_points.evidence: The single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis clearly depicted the molecular structure of PyDI-C6 to possess a completely rigid and planar polycyclic scaffold... A short stacking distance of 3.20 Å evidences very strong π-π interactions among the molecules.

knowledge_points.content: Regioselective dihalogenation of 1,5,6,10-PyDI occurs at the 3 and 8 positions in the non-K regions, allowing for the synthesis of regioregular conjugated polymers via cross-coupling.
knowledge_points.evidence: Moreover, this molecule undergoes regioselective dihalogenation to afford a 3,8-dibromosubstituted derivative, which may conveniently be incorporated into conjugated polymers via crosscoupling with suitable comonomers.

knowledge_points.content: The conjugated polymer PyDI-TT, composed of alternating PyDI and bithiophene units, achieved an optimal electron mobility of 0.335 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ in organic field-effect transistors.
knowledge_points.evidence: An optimal electron mobility of 0.335 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ is achieved by PyDI-TT, which clearly demonstrates the potential of 1,5,6,10-PyDI as a potent building block.

knowledge_points.content: 1,5,6,10-PyDI-based polymers exhibit C–H···O hydrogen bonding between aromatic protons on the pyrene skeleton and imide carbonyl oxygen atoms, with measured distances of 2.5–2.6 Å.
knowledge_points.evidence: C-H-O type hydrogen bonding (H-bonding) interactions are observed between molecules from neighboring stacks... Short distances of 2.5-2.6 Å are measured between the aromatic protons on the pyrene skeleton and the imide carbonyl oxygen atoms.

knowledge_points.content: The OFETs were fabricated in a top-gate/bottom-contact (TG/BC) configuration using a CYTOP fluoropolymer (ca. 500 nm thick) as the dielectric layer to protect the active layer from moisture and oxygen.
knowledge_points.evidence: Using an amorphous fluoropolymer (CYTOP, ca. 500 nm thick) as the dielectric layer and phenylethanethioltreated Au electrodes, a top-gate/bottom-contact (TG/BC) device configuration was used.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis of PyDI-TT thin films shows a $\pi-\pi$ stacking distance of 3.7 Å and a bimodal texture consisting of both edge-on and face-on crystallite orientations.
knowledge_points.evidence: For PyDI-TT... the π-π stacking distance calculated from the (010) peak is about 3.7 Å... long-range diffraction (h00) and π-π stacking (010) peaks are both observed in the out-of-plane direction, suggesting the mixed edge-on and face-on orientations.

knowledge_points.content: PyDI-T and PyDI-TT polymers demonstrate high thermal stability with decomposition temperatures exceeding 400 °C as determined by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
knowledge_points.evidence: Thermogravimetric analyses (TGA) reveal the excellent thermal stability of the two polymers, with decomposition temperatures of over 400 °C.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations indicate that the PyDI-based polymers have improved backbone planarity compared to NDI and PDI analogues due to smaller calculated dihedral angles between the PyDI and thiophene units.
knowledge_points.evidence: Additionally, the dihedral angles between the PyDI and thiophene units in PyDI-T and PyDI-TT are calculated to be smaller compared to those exhibited by the NDI- and PDI-based polymer analogues, suggesting improved backbone planarity.

knowledge_points.content: The electron mobility of PyDI-TT was optimized by annealing the thin films at 180 °C, which enhanced the current modulation to 10⁴–10⁵.
knowledge_points.evidence: Remarkably, upon annealing at 180 °C the thin film of PyDI-TT exhibits an electron mobility of up to 0.335 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ with good current modulation (10⁴–10⁵).
